reviewer: Grok (independent read-only review of the libSystem spawn-attribute fix; did not rebuild)
verdict: The semantic claim holds. Exports, imports, and file size match canonical libSystem 8ff49e0c. Section headers match except __text, which grows by 0x14. After normalizing branch, adr, adrp, and adrp+add targets, the only new __text instructions are the five-instruction memset in _posix_spawnattr_init. Several non-text sections are not byte-identical; their checked differences are 0x14 layout fixups, and __unwind_info was not fully decoded. This is not a runtime proof that the SIGKILL is fixed.
patch: The patch is 580 bytes and inserts memset(*psattrp, 0, sizeof(struct _posix_spawnattr)) immediately after a successful malloc and before the existing defaults in posix_spawnattr_init. No other line changes. Applied with patch -p1 onto a temporary copy of the baseline file. source_before d008092c797ebaa7828c59abfbbf27d4d183174455db1e4eedc66f0bc8d15d03 and source_after 932b15200d56006f771b0838f386c4d35a496c30f4e1ab35f488e78bee1710e2 match the build record. The repository source was not modified.

binary_comparison.file_size: Both files are 4202078 bytes. Canonical sha256 is 8ff49e0c2a5f1c6532101c7ed662632444cc97ae9669479090e7968deddd12ff, dumped read-only from the candidate-004 ramdisk.
binary_comparison.symbols: llvm-nm --defined-only yields the same name-and-type multiset on both files (8421 address-bearing rows). Every address follows one rule: if the old address is below 0xa89c8 the new address is 0x14 lower, otherwise it is unchanged. 2237 symbols move and 6184 stay, with zero exceptions. _posix_spawnattr_init moves from 0xa8988 to 0xa8974. _malloc stays at 0x18b718 and _memset stays at 0xbbf00. llvm-nm -u yields the same 70 undefined names. No export or import was added or removed.
binary_comparison.section_headers: Both files have 30 sections. The only header change is __TEXT,__text: address 0x51e0 to 0x51cc, size 0x2673dc to 0x2673f0. That is 20 bytes, five instructions. The byte at 0x26c5bc remains the end of __text, so __stubs still starts at the same address.
binary_comparison.text: The stable tail from 0xa89c8 to the end of __text is 462589 words, with 603 PC-relative retargets into the moved prefix and zero semantic mismatches. In the moved prefix, 126 add-immediate instructions drop their immediate by exactly 0x14. One adrp+add pair crosses a page: old address 0x3b010 becomes 0x3affc, a drop of 0x14. The malloc-success CBNZ keeps the encoding 0xb50000a0; its target moves from the old success path at 0xa89c8 to 0xa89b4, which is the first instruction of the inserted memset. The error epilogue branch changes from 0x14000064 to 0x14000069 so both still land on absolute 0xa8b54. The fallthrough branch at 0xa8b50 stays 0x14000001 and also lands on 0xa8b54. The five inserted words at 0xa89b4 are ldr x8,[sp,#0x10]; ldr x0,[x8]; mov x2,#0xf8; mov w1,#0; bl 0xbbf00 (_memset). The next word, at 0xa89c8 in both files, is the original success-path ldr. The record's 618519-versus-618524 objdump counts were not re-counted; the check above is the byte-level one.
binary_comparison.other_sections: Address and size match for every section except __text. The bytes do not all match. __objc_selrefs is identical (232 bytes). __init_offsets differs in 3 bytes, two 4-byte values each smaller by 0x14. __objc_methlist differs in 5 bytes, each smaller by 0x14 (0x30 to 0x1c, 0x3c to 0x28, 0x54 to 0x40, 0x70 to 0x5c, 0x8c to 0x78). __DATA_CONST,__const differs in 297 bytes; every run is an aligned value smaller by 0x14. __DATA,__data differs in 13 bytes, the same way. __unwind_info differs in 846 bytes; two runs match an 8-byte pointer smaller by 0x14 and 792 runs do not. Samples there are single bytes that increase by 0x14, which fits a compressed offset fixup and was not fully decoded. __common and __bss are zerofill (file offset 0) and have no file bytes to compare. The user's 'every section except __text' claim holds for the section headers and does not hold for raw bytes.

spawner_risk: Every caller of posix_spawnattr_init in this libSystem receives zeros for the fields that function never wrote, including the port, file-descriptor, and kq limits and the other fields past the stores that already existed. The existing stores still run after the memset, so flags, signals, binprefs, ports, jetsam, persona, and the other fields the function already set keep those defaults. malloc and memset both use 248 bytes (the binary immediate is 0xf8), so the memset covers the allocation and does not run past it. The kernel applies a port or file-descriptor limit only when the value is greater than 0, so a zero limit is the do-not-apply default. Callers that set fields after init are unchanged. The behavior change is for a spawner that was depending on heap garbage in an unwritten field, which is the bug under review. That includes launchd, the desktop's spawn path, and the app's /bin/sh when they call posix_spawnattr_init in this library. It does not prove the first-app SIGKILL is fixed, and it does not change a spawner that sets an explicit nonzero limit after init.
